newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean workers refuse to handle food for N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean workers refuse to handle food for N.Korea.

text.p: South Korean workers in the western port of Inchon said on Thursday they would not handle food shipments to impoverished North Korea unless the Stalinist state showed it was ready to change.

"Unless the North Korean regime gives up its efforts to invade the South, attend the four-party peace talks, and change its policy we refuse to load any food shipments being sent to the North," the Inchon Port and Transport Workers Union said in a statement.
Many South Koreans have been keen to help their brethren in the North, which is on the verge of famine, and donations have flowed into the South Korean Red Cross.
Officials from the South Korean Red Cross, which is the only window for sending private aid to the North, said they were unaware of the union's decision.

According to a union official at Inchon, there were no current food shipments scheduled to be sent to the North, but any in the future would be turned away. Most shipments have been sent through the port.
Red Cross officials have said they would begin delivering 15,000 tonnes of corn by train to the North next week.

U.N. and aid officials have been warning for months of a famine in the making in North Korea, which was badly hit by two harvest failures because of heavy rains and flooding in 1995 and 1996 that destroyed roads and crops.
The United States and South Korea insist large-scale aid can only be debated at four-nation peace talks including China.
The talks are aimed at reaching a lasting peace deal to replace a truce that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.

Despite Pyongyang's food woes, a recent high-level defector to Seoul said North Korean leader Kim Jong-il was looking for an opportunity to strike against the South, a parliamentary committee was told last week.

The Inchon union official, who asked not to be identified, said many workers were disenchanted about sending food to the North. A recent questionaire showed 90 percent of 3,010 workers who responded said they were against sending aid.
The port and transport union is a member of the Federation of Korean Trade Unions, South Korea's largest umbrella union.
The federation, which is actively raising funds to help the North, said the Inchon union's decision was made independently.
